203	  the longest browsers keep). Without it the reply is unchanged, so the
204	  CLI and the headset are untouched. `RemoteReply` (`:389`) gains
205	  `set_cookie: Option<String>` and `#[derive(Default)]`; Settled says it
206	  is built literally at about 15 sites in `src/app.rs` and none in `tests/`,
207	  so each literal gets `..RemoteReply::default()`, a mechanical edit.
208	- The cookie goes to every HTTPS service on that host, on any port
209	  (Settled). It is `HttpOnly`, so it cannot be read by script; it can be
210	  sent to a service the owner runs on the same Mac. The dialog says so, and
211	  it is named for the owner at the end.
212	
213	### Decision 3: one QR
214	
215	**One URL.** The pairing window's QR and "Copy invite" carry
216	`https://<ip>:<port>/?code=<code>&key=<spki_sha256>&id=<server_id>`,
217	built by one pure function in `src/core/remote.rs`,
218	`invite_url(address: SocketAddr, identity, code)`. It formats the address
219	through `SocketAddr`, so an IPv6 result gets its brackets (the JSON form
220	did not). Code, key and id are Crockford, hex and a UUID: nothing needs
221	percent-encoding. The JSON form is no longer emitted. Settled: the
222	visionOS paste field, `ConnectionManager.swift`, `BrowserView.swift:106,
223	883` and the CLI all go through `PairingInvite.parse`
224	(`client/Sources/SwitchboardProtocol/Info.swift:114`), so only that
225	changes: it tries `URLComponents` first (`code`, `key`, `id`, and
226	`addresses = ["host:port"]`) and the existing JSON decode second, so an
227	invite copied before the update still pairs. `addresses` stays a list
228	(`ConnectionManager.swift:483`, `main.swift:120`). The `.local` name is not
229	put in the URL: owner question B decides that, and the IP works whichever
230	way it comes back.
231	
232	### Decision 4: the static paths
233	
234	- **Paths, exactly:** `GET /` (also with a query), `GET /app.js`,
235	  `GET /app.css`. Content types `text/html; charset=utf-8`,
236	  `text/javascript; charset=utf-8`, `text/css; charset=utf-8`. The HTML
237	  carries `<link rel="icon" href="data:,">` so no `/favicon.ico` request is
238	  made. Any other method on these is `405` with `Allow: GET`; any other
239	  path outside `/api/v1/` is `404` with the usual JSON error.
240	- **Headers on all three (and the 404/405):** `Content-Security-Policy:
241	  default-src 'none'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; connect-src
242	  'self'; img-src data:; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none';
243	  frame-ancestors 'none'`, `Cache-Control: no-store`,
244	  `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` (the URL with the code must not leave in
245	  a `Referer`), `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Connection: close`.
246	  The page has no inline script, no inline style and no `style=` attribute,
247	  and no external URL. Whether WebKit treats `connect-src 'self'` as
248	  covering `wss://` on the same host is not in the facts; the first
249	  manual run on Safari records it, and the polling path is why a "no" does
250	  not break the page.
251	- **Who answers:** the connection thread (`connection`,
252	  `src/adapters/remote.rs:770`), before the request is handed to the
253	  frame, because the bytes need no core state and §4.1 says the frame does
254	  core state only. The bytes are `include_str!("../../web/index.html")`,
255	  `app.js`, `app.css` in `adapters/remote.rs`. No build step, no
256	  dependency.
257	- **Pool and rate window.** A page load counts against the 4
258	  unauthenticated connections like any stranger (§4.1; unchanged), and
259	  `Connection: close` frees the slot as soon as the file is sent, so the
260	  three files do not hold three slots for 30 s of idle (Unresolved 8: how
261	  many parallel connections iOS Safari opens needs a device). Static paths get
262	  their own `RateWindow` in `Limits` (`:625-640`), 60 per minute per
263	  listener, `429` past it, so a page-load loop cannot be charged to the
264	  `/pair` window (6/min) or the `/info` window (60/min). The page's own
265	  `/info` and `/pair` calls count against theirs as today.
266	- **Before pairing the listener serves `/info`, `/pair` and the page.**
267	  §5's "Require pairing before anything but `/info` and `/pair`" is
268	  amended to add the page. The page's bytes are identical on every
269	  installation and carry no host data (no id, no key, no name): the
270	  host-specific values arrive only in the URL the owner scanned and in
271	  `/info`.
272	- **Opened with neither code nor marker:** a plain message: "Open
273	  Remote devices in Switchboard on the Mac, choose Allow pairing, and scan
274	  the code with this device's camera." No code-entry form in this cut: a
275	  typed code without the scanned key would skip the one check the page
276	  can make. A paste field is the natural follow-up.
277	- **`refuse` and the code.** The page request never reaches the frame, so
278	  `refuse` (`src/app.rs:3754`, logs method and path only) is not on the
279	  path; the static arm logs nothing and never logs the query.
280	
281	### The page's protocol (`web/app.js`)
282	
283	Order on load: (1) if `location.search` has `code`, hold `code`, `key`,
284	`id` in variables and call `history.replaceState(null, "",
285	location.pathname)` as the first statement; (2) `GET /api/v1/info`;
286	(3) with a code: refuse to continue unless `info.spki_sha256 === key` and
287	`info.server_id === id`, else say "this is not the host whose code was
288	scanned" and send nothing; (4) `POST /api/v1/pair {code, device_name,
289	spki_sha256, transport: "cookie"}`; on success store the marker and
290	continue, on `403 pairing_closed|wrong_code|wrong_key` say which, plainly;
291	(5) with no code and a marker: if `info.server_id` equals the marker's and
292	the key differs, "identity changed, pair again" and send nothing; (6)
293	`GET /api/v1/device` for the name and current scope; a 401 is the revoked
294	or never-paired state above.
295	
296	After that it speaks §4.2 and §4.4: every reply is the envelope
297	`{epoch, revision, body}`; one held revision per resource key (a project's
298	session list, one session, one session's `conversation` or `screen`); a
299	reply is applied only at or past the held revision; a changed `epoch`
300	refetches everything. Subscribe first, then snapshot: open
301	`wss://<host>/api/v1/events`, wait for `hello`, fetch `projects` and each
302	`projects/{id}/sessions` (at most 4 in flight), then apply buffered events
303	by revision. `changed {session}` refetches that session and re-sorts;
304	`changed {sessions, project}` refetches that project; `changed {projects}`
305	refetches the list; `removed` drops it; `resync_required` reconnects and
306	refetches. Opening a session sends `watch {kind: "conversation", id}` for a
307	Claude session or `watch {kind: "screen", id}` otherwise, waits for
308	`watching`, then fetches `last-response` or `screen`; leaving sends
309	`unwatch`. Refetch the open view every 30 s regardless (§4.4, covers
310	eviction). Without the socket, every poll refetches the list and the open
311	view; the held-revision rule is the same.
312	
313	A reply is `POST sessions/{id}/send {op, text}` under `control`, with the
314	op made per command. On a timeout the page asks `GET ops/{op}` and follows
315	§4.5: `done` uses the reply, `interrupted` shows the session's state and
316	never resubmits, `unknown` resubmits with the same op. A session with
317	`trust_question` shows "Waiting at Claude Code's folder trust question;
318	answer it on the Mac" and no box; one with `prompt_refusal` shows the box
319	disabled with that reason. Trust, resume, new session, the draft,
320	dictation, Dispatch tickets and the conversation beyond the last response
321	are not on the page (owner question; the API serves them).
322	
323	### `GET /api/v1/device`
324	
325	Authenticated, any scope. Reply, in the envelope: `{device_id, name,
326	scope, server_id}`, read from the core's current device, so a scope change
327	in the dialog shows on the next call. Handled in `serve_remote`
328	(`src/app.rs:3017`) after `authenticate` and before the allowlist match,
329	beside `events`, with no `wire::Body`. No fixture: Swift does not decode
330	it (the fixtures exist for Swift and Rust to agree, and nothing on the
331	Swift side reads this).
332	
333	## The actions and effects
334	
335	One new action, `AppAction::CertificateReissued { certificate: String,
336	names: Vec<String>, expires: SystemTime }`, handled in
337	`src/core/remote.rs` through the existing `update_identity`
338	(`:105-117`), which already emits `Effect::SaveIdentity` and does nothing
339	when read-only. No new effect, no new port method: `RemoteStore` already
340	saves the identity.
341	
342	Adapter: `remote::reissue_certificate(identity, key_pem, names, now) ->
343	Result<(String, SystemTime), String>` beside `make_identity`
344	(`src/adapters/remote.rs:95`), over `KeyPair::from_pem`, with the SANs,
345	`serverAuth`, `not_before` a day back, `not_after` 800 days out; and
346	`remote::local_names()`, the sorted names above (the `.local` name from
347	`scutil --get LocalHostName`, absent when the command fails or off macOS,
348	so Linux CI compiles and passes). In `bind_remote` (`src/app.rs:2935`),
349	before `tls_config` at `:2957`: if `identity.certificate_names` differs
350	from `local_names()`, or `certificate_expires` is `None` or within 30 days,
351	call `reissue_certificate` with the Keychain key already fetched there,
352	dispatch `CertificateReissued`, and build the TLS config from the core's
353	identity afterwards. `make_identity` also fills the two new fields. An
354	address that changes while the port is running is not noticed until the
355	next bind; that is a known gap in the design status, not machinery here.
356	
357	Serving the page is not an effect: it never leaves the connection thread.
358	The request-side changes (three headers, `set_cookie`, the Origin check)
359	are in the adapter and `authenticate`, with no action.
360	
361	## The UI
362	
363	**The pairing window** (`src/ui/remote.rs:155-215`). The `json!` payload
364	and `qr_texture` input become `core::remote::invite_url(...)`; "Copy
365	invite" copies the URL and its hover says "The QR code's link, to open in
366	a browser or paste into a client". The caption keeps the key and code and
367	gains the trust text from decision 1 (two sentences: the browser will warn
368	about this host's certificate; accepting it is the step that trusts this
369	network and does not verify the host; the key in the link only stops a
370	page from sending the code to a different Switchboard; the link works
371	once and expires in five minutes or three wrong codes). The paired-devices
372	section (`devices`, `:230`) gains one line under the table: a browser's
373	token is an HttpOnly cookie sent to any HTTPS service on this Mac's
374	address. It uses `GAP` and `PAD`; no logic beyond the format call.
375	
376	**The page** (`web/index.html`, `app.js`, `app.css`), one file each, no
377	framework. A header with the host's name (from `/info`), the device's
378	name and scope word (from `/device`), and the live/polling indicator.
379	Below: a "Waiting on you" group first (every session with `waiting`,
380	marked, with `waiting_reason`), then one group per project; each row has
381	the session name, kind, `card` word and the excerpt. A session view with
382	the last response (Claude) or screen text (anything else), refreshed on
383	`changed`, and the reply box under `control`, absent for `read`. States,
384	each one sentence: not paired, pairing closed, wrong host, identity
385	changed, no longer paired, host unreachable, live updates unavailable,
386	`read` scope. Text only, `textContent` never `innerHTML`, since session
387	text is attacker-influenced.
388	
389	## The tests
390	
391	CI cannot drive a browser and the tree has no JS runner (the issue rules
392	out a dependency), so the page's reconcile logic is checked by hand. The
393	host's side is tested in full.
394	
395	- **`src/core/tests.rs`:** `invite_url` for an IPv4 and an IPv6 address;
396	  `CertificateReissued` updates the identity and returns one
397	  `SaveIdentity`; it is a no-op read-only.
398	- **`src/adapters/remote.rs` unit tests:** `reissue_certificate` keeps
399	  `spki_sha256` (`spki_sha256_of_cert` equals the key's) and `tls_config`
400	  accepts it; `RemoteRequest::token` prefers the bearer, reads only the
401	  cookie with the right name, rejects an oversized value; the same-origin
402	  rule (equal, different port, different scheme, missing, case).
403	- **`tests/remote.rs`** (extend `http`, `:245`, to return the headers; keep
404	  the old signature as a wrapper so existing callers do not change):
405	  - the three paths answer unpaired with the exact `Content-Type`, the
406	    CSP above, `Cache-Control: no-store`, `Referrer-Policy`, `nosniff` and
407	    `Connection: close`; `/favicon.ico`, `/web/app.js` and `/%2e%2e/` give
408	    404; `POST /` gives 405; `GET /?code=ABCDEFGH` serves the page and the
409	    frame sees nothing (the port's `poll` returns no request).
410	  - **The embedded page references only paths the host serves:** every
411	    `src`/`href` in the HTML is one of the three paths or the `data:` icon;
412	    no inline `<script>` body, `on…=` or `style=` attribute, no `http(s)://`
413	    URL at all; every `/api/v1/…` literal in `app.js` (a `${…}`
414	    replaced by a UUID) answers anything but `404 not_found` for a
415	    control-scope device.
416	  - **Rate window and pool:** 61 static GETs in a minute give a 429 on the
417	    61st, and `/pair` still answers; ten sequential page loads leave no
418	    unauthenticated slot held, so a pairing right after them works. The
419	    existing `stalled_strangers_fill_their_own_pool_and_never_a_paired_clients`
420	    (`:3226`) stays as is.
421	  - **Cookie transport:** `/pair` with `transport: "cookie"` returns no
422	    `token` and a `Set-Cookie` with each attribute named above and the
423	    per-`server_id` name; the cookie alone then reads `waiting` and
424	    `device`; a `send` with the cookie and no `Origin`, or with another
425	    origin, is `403 forbidden_origin` and sends nothing; with the matching
426	    `Origin` it goes; an upgrade with the cookie and a wrong `Origin` is
427	    403; a bearer request with no `Origin` is unchanged. Pairing without
428	    `transport` returns the token as today.
429	  - **`/device`:** returns the name and scope; after `SetDeviceScope` the
430	    next call shows the new one; after revoke the cookie gets `401
431	    unauthorized` and the socket closes (beside
432	    `revoke_closes_the_devices_socket`, `:2892`).
433	  - **The pairing flow as the CLI does it:** parse `invite_url`'s output,
434	    GET `/info`, compare the key, POST `/pair`, read `/device` and
435	    `/projects`; this is the acceptance flow minus the browser.
436	  - **The reissued certificate:** a rustls client that trusts the
437	    certificate as its own anchor completes a handshake for `ServerName`
438	    `localhost` and for the IP SAN; the existing pinned config connects
439	    unchanged (the pin did not move). If webpki refuses a self-signed leaf as
440	    its own anchor, the implementer asserts the SANs another way (a dev
441	    dependency that decodes the DER, named in the commit) rather than
442	    dropping the test.
443	- **`tests/ui.rs`** (beside `remote_devices_dialog_opens_pairing_and_revokes_a_device`,
444	  `:7424`): with a pairing window seeded, the dialog shows the trust text,
445	  the key and code, and "Copy invite" with `record_actions` copies a text
446	  that starts `https://` and carries `code=`.
447	- **Swift** (`client/Tests`): `PairingInvite.parse` of a URL (IPv4, IPv6
448	  with brackets, missing `code`), of the old JSON, and of garbage; the
449	  CLI usage text. Run `swift test` in `client/` where the toolchain is
450	  present.
451	- **By hand, once, recorded in the design status:** the issue's
452	  acceptance on a phone: scan, accept the warning, see the sessions, a
453	  session starting to wait moves to the top without a reload, a reply
454	  arrives, revoke in the dialog and the next request says so. Order:
455	  (1) the cookie test of decision 2 first; (2) whether `new WebSocket`
456	  connects (Owner A); (3) the pool during the page load (Unresolved 8);
457	  (4) `connect-src 'self'` and `wss`. With
458	  `SWITCHBOARD_DATA_DIR` short, `SWITCHBOARD_REMOTE_PORT` set, and the
459	  script lines `remote-listen lan <port>` and `pairing <code>` (no new
460	  script line is needed).
461	
462	## Order of work and docs (one commit; the app runs at each step)
463	
464	1. `RemoteRequest`/`RemoteReply` fields, `token`, the Origin rule,
465	   `/device`, `transport: "cookie"` (native paths unchanged).
466	2. Static paths on the connection thread, the rate window, the 404 for
467	   strays; `web/` files as a stub page that loads.
468	3. `Identity` fields, `reissue_certificate`, `bind_remote`.
469	4. `invite_url`, the dialog, `PairingInvite.parse`, the CLI usage text.
470	5. The page.
471	6. Docs: `docs/remote-client.md` §4.1 (static pool and window,
472	   `Connection: close`), §4.3 (table rows for the page and `/device`), §5
473	   (QR is a URL, the browser trust step and what the key check does not
474	   prove, the cookie, the Origin rule, the reissue); `docs/design.md`
475	   "Remote client" status (what is built, plus the gaps: address change
476	   while running, no code-entry form, no `.local` URL, polling when `wss`
477	   fails, the manual run's findings); `README.md` Layout rows for `web/*`
478	   and the changed rows for `remote.rs` (core, adapters, ui) and
479	   `tests/remote.rs`, the dev-aid text for "Copy invite" (now a link; the
480	   CLI still takes it) in the `SWITCHBOARD_REMOTE_PORT` entry;
481	   `client/README.md` for the CLI's argument; `CHANGELOG.md` Unreleased:
482	   "The remote port serves a web page: scan the pairing window's QR code
483	   with a phone to see the sessions, which are waiting, and to reply."
484	
485	## For the owner (follow-ups, not in this commit)
486	
487	- **A (Safari, `wss`):** if the phone run shows `wss://` fails after the
488	  warning, install-the-certificate (a download route or a profile) is the
489	  follow-up. It is a second trust mechanism and changes §5.
490	- **B (`.local`):** if `https://<name>.local:<port>/` resolves from the
491	  phone, put it in the URL. The certificate already carries it.
492	- **D (cookie):** if the cookie fails on `fetch` in Safari with an IP
493	  host, the fallback is a follow-up decision, not a second transport here.
494	- Cookie reach across ports on one host (Settled): is it acceptable, or
495	  should the page move to a `.local` name so the cookie is host-scoped to
496	  one name?
497	- A code-entry form, and Dispatch tickets, trust, resume, new session and
498	  the draft on the page.
499	
500	## Commit message
501	
502	`Serve a browser page on the remote port: pairing by link, cookie token, a /device read, a reissued certificate`
503	
504	## Contract additions
505	
506	- `RemoteRequest` (adapter, not the shared contract): `cookie`, `origin`,
507	  `host` and `token()`; `RemoteReply`: `set_cookie` and `Default`.
508	- `GET /api/v1/device` → `{device_id, name, scope, server_id}` (spec §4.3).
509	- `POST /api/v1/pair` request field `transport` (`"cookie"`); reply omits
510	  `token` and sets `Set-Cookie: __Host-sb-<server_id>`.
511	- Error code `forbidden_origin` (403).
512	- Static `GET /`, `/app.js`, `/app.css` on the remote port (spec §4.1, §5).
513	- `Identity.certificate_names`, `Identity.certificate_expires` (both
514	  `#[serde(default)]`); `IDENTITY_SCHEMA_VERSION` = the value in
515	  `src/ports/remote.rs` at implementation time, plus one.
516	- `AppAction::CertificateReissued { certificate, names, expires }`; no new
517	  `Effect`.
518	- `core::remote::invite_url`; `remote::reissue_certificate`,
519	  `remote::local_names`.
520	- Pairing QR payload: an `https://` link replaces the JSON object;
521	  `PairingInvite.parse` (Swift) accepts both.
522	- No `model.rs`, `SessionView`, `control/` or fixture change.

# Plan: a web control surface on the remote port (#230)

Line numbers are as they are in this worktree at 7fe8949. Schema versions
as they stand today: `SCHEMA_VERSION = 16` (`src/core/model.rs:12`),
`VIEWS_SCHEMA_VERSION = 7` (`:612`), `IDENTITY_SCHEMA_VERSION = 1`
(`src/ports/remote.rs:17`). Only the last moves, and it is written below
as "the value in `ports/remote.rs` at implementation time, plus one".
"Facts" means the facts file for this issue; a line cited as Settled N or
Unresolved N is in it.

## Where this departs from the issue

- **"The one-line excerpt the card shows" is not on the wire.**
  `SessionView` (`control/src/lib.rs:636-688`) has no excerpt. The record
  has `last_message` (written by `src/bin/switchboard-hook.rs:37`;
  Settled, tree), but `remote-client.md` §4.3 says the excerpt is
  "masked from the turn's full text, then cut", and masking resolves the
  session's secret set, which §4.1 keeps off the frame. Putting
  `last_message` on `SessionView` would send unmasked text from a frame
  answer. So no `SessionView` change: the page fetches
  `sessions/{id}/last-response` for each Claude session, as the headset
  does (`client/Sources/SwitchboardUI/BrowserView.swift:149-163`), and
  only when that session's `last_stop_at_ms` differs from what it holds.
  No `watch` is registered for these, so the 128-key watch set is not
  touched by the list. Codex, shell, command and service rows show kind
  and state without an excerpt.
- **"The device's scope in the header": no endpoint returns it after
  pairing** (`remote_info`, `src/app.rs:3568`, is unauthenticated; the
  `/pair` reply is the only place, and it goes stale when the owner
  changes the scope in the dialog). The plan adds one authenticated read,
  `GET /api/v1/device`. This is the single new read model; the page
  cannot show a current scope without it.
- **"Revoked said plainly" cannot be told from "never paired" by the
  host's answer.** `authenticate` (`src/app.rs:3127-3153`) refuses both
  with `401 unauthorized`, and with an HttpOnly cookie the page cannot
  see whether it holds a token. The page keeps a non-secret marker
  (`server_id`, `device_id`, key hash, name) in `localStorage`. A 401
  with a marker says "This browser is no longer paired (it was revoked on
  the host, or the browser dropped its cookie). Pair again." A 401 with
  no marker says how to pair. "Identity changed, pair again" is the
  marker's `server_id` matching `/info` with a different key hash.
  No new refusal code.
- **"Any path outside `/api/v1/` is refused" is true but late:**
  `serve_remote` refuses it at `src/app.rs:3023`, after the request has
  taken a slot in the 64-deep channel and a frame pass. With a page, a
  browser sends strays (`/favicon.ico`, a prefetch). The connection
  thread now owns this decision: the three page paths are served there, any
  other path outside `/api/v1/` is answered 404 there, and `serve_remote`
  keeps its own refusal as the backstop.
- **"The browser then trusts that certificate for that address" is not
  safe to build on.** Settled (WebKit 41419, code-server's iPad doc): on
  Safari a click-through can cover the page and `fetch` but not `wss://`.
  The page therefore works on REST polling alone and treats the socket as
  an upgrade (decision 1 below).
- **"`history.replaceState` … the code never stays in the history" is
  stronger than the sources.** MDN (Settled) says `replaceState`
  replaces the current entry; it says nothing of what the browser
  recorded before the script ran (Unresolved 6). The plan makes the
  claim the host can keep: the code is single-use and the window closes
  at the first pairing, three failures or five minutes (Settled,
  `src/core/remote.rs:46-72`), so a recorded URL is dead. The dialog says
  that instead of promising the history is clean.

## The record

No new record kind, no `model.rs` change, no `SCHEMA_VERSION` or
`VIEWS_SCHEMA_VERSION` bump. A browser is one more `PairedDevice`
(`src/ports/remote.rs:96-107`) in `devices.json`, which is a bare
`Vec<PairedDevice>` with no version. Its name is the page's `device_name`
("Safari on iPhone", built by the page from `navigator.userAgent`; the
host already cuts it to 64 characters, `new_device`,
`src/core/remote.rs:166-175`). No `kind` field: the name is enough for
the dialog (decision 6) and the host reads no `User-Agent`. Revoke and
scope change already apply on the next request and revoke closes the
socket.

One record changes: `identity.json`. The certificate is reissued over the
same key (Settled: `KeyPair::from_pem` is already used,
`src/adapters/remote.rs:139,146`; the SPKI is of the key, so the pin
and `spki_sha256` do not move, §5). The reason is Settled (Apple's
rules): the current certificate has no subjectAltName, a CN only, no EKU,
and a `not_after` in the year 4096, so it meets none of the SAN, EKU or
825-day rules Safari applies. Reissuing cannot hurt the click-through
path and may help it (Unresolved 1, 2 and 3 are the open questions about
how much), so it does not wait on them. Two additive fields on `Identity`
(`src/ports/remote.rs:26-42`), both `#[serde(default)]`:

- `certificate_names: Vec<String>`: the DNS and IP names the certificate
  carries, sorted.
- `certificate_expires: Option<SystemTime>`.

Bump `IDENTITY_SCHEMA_VERSION` to the value in `ports/remote.rs` at
implementation time, plus one. `identity.json` has no migration step:
`load_identity` is a plain deserialize, so an older file reads with the
defaults (an empty list, `None`), which `bind_remote` treats as "reissue
now". Written through the existing atomic `RemoteFiles::save`.

Rehydration is unchanged: `IdentityLoaded` at launch, devices by token
hash on every request. The pairing window stays non-durable. On the
device, what persists is the HttpOnly cookie (script cannot read it) and
the marker in `localStorage` (not secret: ids and a public key hash).
The cookie is the only place the token lives in the browser (decision 2).

## The signals

### Decision 1: browser trust in the certificate

**Picked: the click-through on the local network is the trust step, said
in the dialog. The host does not offer the certificate for download in
this cut.** Why: a download or profile install is a second trust
mechanism with its own surface (a route that serves a certificate before
pairing, a profile format, what iOS asks of a manually trusted
certificate), and the only evidence that it fixes `wss://` on Safari is
two sources of 2021 and 2026 (Settled), against Unresolved 1-3, which no
experiment here can settle. It is the follow-up if owner question A
comes back unfavourable (named at the end).

What the click-through buys, and what it does not (the dialog says this
in two sentences, and §5 of the spec is amended to say it):

- It lets the owner open the page. It proves nothing about who answered.
- The `key` in the URL lets the genuine page refuse to send the code to a
  host whose `/info` presents a different `spki_sha256`. That catches the
  right page on the wrong genuine host (a second installation on that
  address or port, a rotated key). A page served by an impostor is not a
  genuine page and checks nothing; a page cannot read the key of the TLS
  connection it is on, so even the genuine check proves only that the host
  claims that key. §5's sentence "a relayed request through a substituted
  certificate fails" stands for native clients and is amended: it does not
  hold for a browser.
- What bounds the damage: the code is single-use and short-lived
  (Settled), the pairing window shows scope, and the owner sees the new
  device in the dialog and can revoke it.

The reissue (above) gives the certificate `serverAuth`, a validity of 800
days (under 825, Unresolved 3: if the rule does not bind a manually
trusted leaf, nothing is lost), and SANs for `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`,
the outward address from `local_address()` as an IP SAN, and, on macOS,
`<LocalHostName>.local` as a DNS SAN (Unresolved 2 and 9: both forms are
present, so whichever Safari accepts is there). The dialog says the
certificate is renewed (key, and so pin, unchanged) and that a changed
address means a new browser warning (Unresolved 7).

The page's default is REST polling every 5 seconds plus a refetch of the
open session. When `new WebSocket` opens, the page switches to events
and stops polling; when it fails or closes, the page says "Live updates
unavailable, refreshing every 5 s" and polls. This is the same page
whether Unresolved 1 comes back favourable or not; the socket is the
enhancement, built behind the polling and not in front of it.
`crypto.randomUUID` is used only when `window.isSecureContext`, with a
`getRandomValues` fallback otherwise (Unresolved 4).

### Decision 2: how the token reaches the host

**Picked: an `HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict` cookie, set by the
`/pair` reply, carried by `fetch` and by the socket handshake. The page's
script never sees the token. Nothing in `localStorage`, no subprotocol
token.** That is the safer store (a script on the origin can read
`localStorage`; it cannot read an HttpOnly cookie), so it is the one this
plan builds. The facts file's Owner D says the server accepts all three
transports; this plan builds one (plus the bearer header the native
clients use) and does not build the other two.

Mechanics that are unresolved are the implementer's first test, before
any other page code (Unresolved 5): on Safari, Chrome and Firefox with the
reissued certificate, does a `Secure` cookie set by `/pair` over an IP
host come back on a same-origin `fetch`? (This is the basic behaviour; the
`__Host-` prefix needs `Secure`, `Path=/`, no `Domain`, all met.) Does it
come back on a same-origin `new WebSocket` handshake? If the `fetch` half
fails, the finding goes to the owner as a follow-up and no
`localStorage` or subprotocol transport is added in this commit. If only
the socket half fails, nothing changes: the page polls (decision 1).

Host side:

- `read_request` (`src/adapters/remote.rs:444-513`) keeps three more
  headers, as the bearer is kept, so none are logged with the rest:
  `cookie`, `origin`, `host`. `RemoteRequest` (`:360`) gains
  `cookie: Option<String>`, `origin: Option<String>`,
  `host: Option<String>`. Settled: only `adapters/remote.rs` builds it,
  and no test constructs it.
- The token is the bearer if present, else the cookie named
  `__Host-sb-<server_id>` (per-installation name: Settled says cookies are
  not isolated by port, so two instances on one Mac would otherwise
  collide). `authenticate` (`src/app.rs:3127`) takes it from a new
  `RemoteRequest::token(&self, server_id)`; the cookie value is checked
  for length and base64url characters before it is hashed.
- **Origin check.** A cookie is ambient: `SameSite=Strict` is by site, and
  a site includes every port on the host, so another page on another port
  of this Mac is same-site. For a request authenticated by the cookie (no
  bearer), any method but GET and any WebSocket upgrade must carry an
  `Origin` equal to `https://` + the request's `Host` header, compared
  case-insensitively; otherwise `403 forbidden_origin`, no side effect.
  Comparing with the `Host` header, not a list of addresses, is what makes
  this correct for an IP, a `.local` name or loopback. Bearer-authenticated
  requests are exempt: a header is not ambient. This answers the owner
  question on `Origin`, and it is a security decision, so it is decided
  here.
- **`/pair`** (`remote_pair`, `src/app.rs:3606`) takes an additive body
  field `"transport": "cookie"`. With it the reply omits `token`, and
  `RemoteReply` carries `Set-Cookie: __Host-sb-<server_id>=<token>;
  Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Max-Age=34560000` (400 days,
  the longest browsers keep). Without it the reply is unchanged, so the
  CLI and the headset are untouched. `RemoteReply` (`:389`) gains
  `set_cookie: Option<String>` and `#[derive(Default)]`; Settled says it
  is built literally at about 15 sites in `src/app.rs` and none in `tests/`,
  so each literal gets `..RemoteReply::default()`, a mechanical edit.
- The cookie goes to every HTTPS service on that host, on any port
  (Settled). It is `HttpOnly`, so it cannot be read by script; it can be
  sent to a service the owner runs on the same Mac. The dialog says so, and
  it is named for the owner at the end.

### Decision 3: one QR

**One URL.** The pairing window's QR and "Copy invite" carry
`https://<ip>:<port>/?code=<code>&key=<spki_sha256>&id=<server_id>`,
built by one pure function in `src/core/remote.rs`,
`invite_url(address: SocketAddr, identity, code)`. It formats the address
through `SocketAddr`, so an IPv6 result gets its brackets (the JSON form
did not). Code, key and id are Crockford, hex and a UUID: nothing needs
percent-encoding. The JSON form is no longer emitted. Settled: the
visionOS paste field, `ConnectionManager.swift`, `BrowserView.swift:106,
883` and the CLI all go through `PairingInvite.parse`
(`client/Sources/SwitchboardProtocol/Info.swift:114`), so only that
changes: it tries `URLComponents` first (`code`, `key`, `id`, and
`addresses = ["host:port"]`) and the existing JSON decode second, so an
invite copied before the update still pairs. `addresses` stays a list
(`ConnectionManager.swift:483`, `main.swift:120`). The `.local` name is not
put in the URL: owner question B decides that, and the IP works whichever
way it comes back.

### Decision 4: the static paths

- **Paths, exactly:** `GET /` (also with a query), `GET /app.js`,
  `GET /app.css`. Content types `text/html; charset=utf-8`,
  `text/javascript; charset=utf-8`, `text/css; charset=utf-8`. The HTML
  carries `<link rel="icon" href="data:,">` so no `/favicon.ico` request is
  made. Any other method on these is `405` with `Allow: GET`; any other
  path outside `/api/v1/` is `404` with the usual JSON error.
- **Headers on all three (and the 404/405):** `Content-Security-Policy:
  default-src 'none'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; connect-src
  'self'; img-src data:; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none';
  frame-ancestors 'none'`, `Cache-Control: no-store`,
  `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` (the URL with the code must not leave in
  a `Referer`), `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Connection: close`.
  The page has no inline script, no inline style and no `style=` attribute,
  and no external URL. Whether WebKit treats `connect-src 'self'` as
  covering `wss://` on the same host is not in the facts; the first
  manual run on Safari records it, and the polling path is why a "no" does
  not break the page.
- **Who answers:** the connection thread (`connection`,
  `src/adapters/remote.rs:770`), before the request is handed to the
  frame, because the bytes need no core state and §4.1 says the frame does
  core state only. The bytes are `include_str!("../../web/index.html")`,
  `app.js`, `app.css` in `adapters/remote.rs`. No build step, no
  dependency.
- **Pool and rate window.** A page load counts against the 4
  unauthenticated connections like any stranger (§4.1; unchanged), and
  `Connection: close` frees the slot as soon as the file is sent, so the
  three files do not hold three slots for 30 s of idle (Unresolved 8: how
  many parallel connections iOS Safari opens needs a device). Static paths get
  their own `RateWindow` in `Limits` (`:625-640`), 60 per minute per
  listener, `429` past it, so a page-load loop cannot be charged to the
  `/pair` window (6/min) or the `/info` window (60/min). The page's own
  `/info` and `/pair` calls count against theirs as today.
- **Before pairing the listener serves `/info`, `/pair` and the page.**
  §5's "Require pairing before anything but `/info` and `/pair`" is
  amended to add the page. The page's bytes are identical on every
  installation and carry no host data (no id, no key, no name): the
  host-specific values arrive only in the URL the owner scanned and in
  `/info`.
- **Opened with neither code nor marker:** a plain message: "Open
  Remote devices in Switchboard on the Mac, choose Allow pairing, and scan
  the code with this device's camera." No code-entry form in this cut: a
  typed code without the scanned key would skip the one check the page
  can make. A paste field is the natural follow-up.
- **`refuse` and the code.** The page request never reaches the frame, so
  `refuse` (`src/app.rs:3754`, logs method and path only) is not on the
  path; the static arm logs nothing and never logs the query.

### The page's protocol (`web/app.js`)

Order on load: (1) if `location.search` has `code`, hold `code`, `key`,
`id` in variables and call `history.replaceState(null, "",
location.pathname)` as the first statement; (2) `GET /api/v1/info`;
(3) with a code: refuse to continue unless `info.spki_sha256 === key` and
`info.server_id === id`, else say "this is not the host whose code was
scanned" and send nothing; (4) `POST /api/v1/pair {code, device_name,
spki_sha256, transport: "cookie"}`; on success store the marker and
continue, on `403 pairing_closed|wrong_code|wrong_key` say which, plainly;
(5) with no code and a marker: if `info.server_id` equals the marker's and
the key differs, "identity changed, pair again" and send nothing; (6)
`GET /api/v1/device` for the name and current scope; a 401 is the revoked
or never-paired state above.

After that it speaks §4.2 and §4.4: every reply is the envelope
`{epoch, revision, body}`; one held revision per resource key (a project's
session list, one session, one session's `conversation` or `screen`); a
reply is applied only at or past the held revision; a changed `epoch`
refetches everything. Subscribe first, then snapshot: open
`wss://<host>/api/v1/events`, wait for `hello`, fetch `projects` and each
`projects/{id}/sessions` (at most 4 in flight), then apply buffered events
by revision. `changed {session}` refetches that session and re-sorts;
`changed {sessions, project}` refetches that project; `changed {projects}`
refetches the list; `removed` drops it; `resync_required` reconnects and
refetches. Opening a session sends `watch {kind: "conversation", id}` for a
Claude session or `watch {kind: "screen", id}` otherwise, waits for
`watching`, then fetches `last-response` or `screen`; leaving sends
`unwatch`. Refetch the open view every 30 s regardless (§4.4, covers
eviction). Without the socket, every poll refetches the list and the open
view; the held-revision rule is the same.

A reply is `POST sessions/{id}/send {op, text}` under `control`, with the
op made per command. On a timeout the page asks `GET ops/{op}` and follows
§4.5: `done` uses the reply, `interrupted` shows the session's state and
never resubmits, `unknown` resubmits with the same op. A session with
`trust_question` shows "Waiting at Claude Code's folder trust question;
answer it on the Mac" and no box; one with `prompt_refusal` shows the box
disabled with that reason. Trust, resume, new session, the draft,
dictation, Dispatch tickets and the conversation beyond the last response
are not on the page (owner question; the API serves them).

### `GET /api/v1/device`

Authenticated, any scope. Reply, in the envelope: `{device_id, name,
scope, server_id}`, read from the core's current device, so a scope change
in the dialog shows on the next call. Handled in `serve_remote`
(`src/app.rs:3017`) after `authenticate` and before the allowlist match,
beside `events`, with no `wire::Body`. No fixture: Swift does not decode
it (the fixtures exist for Swift and Rust to agree, and nothing on the
Swift side reads this).

## The actions and effects

One new action, `AppAction::CertificateReissued { certificate: String,
names: Vec<String>, expires: SystemTime }`, handled in
`src/core/remote.rs` through the existing `update_identity`
(`:105-117`), which already emits `Effect::SaveIdentity` and does nothing
when read-only. No new effect, no new port method: `RemoteStore` already
saves the identity.

Adapter: `remote::reissue_certificate(identity, key_pem, names, now) ->
Result<(String, SystemTime), String>` beside `make_identity`
(`src/adapters/remote.rs:95`), over `KeyPair::from_pem`, with the SANs,
`serverAuth`, `not_before` a day back, `not_after` 800 days out; and
`remote::local_names()`, the sorted names above (the `.local` name from
`scutil --get LocalHostName`, absent when the command fails or off macOS,
so Linux CI compiles and passes). In `bind_remote` (`src/app.rs:2935`),
before `tls_config` at `:2957`: if `identity.certificate_names` differs
from `local_names()`, or `certificate_expires` is `None` or within 30 days,
call `reissue_certificate` with the Keychain key already fetched there,
dispatch `CertificateReissued`, and build the TLS config from the core's
identity afterwards. `make_identity` also fills the two new fields. An
address that changes while the port is running is not noticed until the
next bind; that is a known gap in the design status, not machinery here.

Serving the page is not an effect: it never leaves the connection thread.
The request-side changes (three headers, `set_cookie`, the Origin check)
are in the adapter and `authenticate`, with no action.

## The UI

**The pairing window** (`src/ui/remote.rs:155-215`). The `json!` payload
and `qr_texture` input become `core::remote::invite_url(...)`; "Copy
invite" copies the URL and its hover says "The QR code's link, to open in
a browser or paste into a client". The caption keeps the key and code and
gains the trust text from decision 1 (two sentences: the browser will warn
about this host's certificate; accepting it is the step that trusts this
network and does not verify the host; the key in the link only stops a
page from sending the code to a different Switchboard; the link works
once and expires in five minutes or three wrong codes). The paired-devices
section (`devices`, `:230`) gains one line under the table: a browser's
token is an HttpOnly cookie sent to any HTTPS service on this Mac's
address. It uses `GAP` and `PAD`; no logic beyond the format call.

**The page** (`web/index.html`, `app.js`, `app.css`), one file each, no
framework. A header with the host's name (from `/info`), the device's
name and scope word (from `/device`), and the live/polling indicator.
Below: a "Waiting on you" group first (every session with `waiting`,
marked, with `waiting_reason`), then one group per project; each row has
the session name, kind, `card` word and the excerpt. A session view with
the last response (Claude) or screen text (anything else), refreshed on
`changed`, and the reply box under `control`, absent for `read`. States,
each one sentence: not paired, pairing closed, wrong host, identity
changed, no longer paired, host unreachable, live updates unavailable,
`read` scope. Text only, `textContent` never `innerHTML`, since session
text is attacker-influenced.

CI cannot drive a browser and the tree has no JS runner (the issue rules

host's side is tested in full.

- **`src/core/tests.rs`:** `invite_url` for an IPv4 and an IPv6 address;

- **`tests/remote.rs`** (extend `http`, `:245`, to return the headers; keep

## For the owner (follow-ups, not in this commit)

- **A (Safari, `wss`):** if the phone run shows `wss://` fails after the

## Commit message

`Serve a browser page on the remote port: pairing by link, cookie token, a /device read, a reissued certificate`

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

1	1. **The card excerpt (plan lines 13-26): the plan changes a decision the spec already made, and the premise it gives in support is false in the tree.**
2	   - **What the spec says.** `docs/remote-client.md:207` says what the excerpt is: "The compact card's one-line excerpt is not part of it [`session.last_response`]: that is `last_message` from the `Stop` hook on the record, a field of the session's metadata, and moves with `changed {session}`." Line 201 says it is masked before it is cut.
3	   - **What the plan does.** It swaps that excerpt for a per-session `GET sessions/{id}/last-response`, which is a projection of the `conversation` key, and so changes the excerpt's identity and the event that refreshes it. The issue asks for "the one-line excerpt the card shows". It does not ask to change what that excerpt is.
4	   - **The masking concern holds.** The tree supports it: the policy is resolved on the worker, not the frame (`src/app.rs:1822-1826`, `docs/remote-client.md:463`). The answer to it is to mask `last_message` the way the spec requires. Redefining the excerpt does not answer it.
5	   - **The supporting premise is false.** The plan says "No `watch` is registered for these, so the 128-key watch set is not touched by the list." In the tree, every content read calls `touch_watch` (`src/app.rs:2111`). That inserts the key into `self.watches` for a minute (`src/app.rs:1754-1768`), and past `WATCH_CAP` the least recently read keys are evicted (`:1789-1798`). So a page polling a list of Claude sessions does fill the shared watch set and can evict a headset's keys.
6	   - **The cost is also missing.** Each first fetch is a whole-transcript parse on the one content worker (§4.1, where Spike 22 measured a 575 MB peak). The plan does not count that.
7	   - **What to do.** Either carry `last_message`, masked, as §4.3 says, or ship rows without an excerpt and name that as a gap. Do not redefine the excerpt.
8	
9	2. **The test "every `/api/v1/…` literal in `app.js` (a `${…}` replaced by a UUID) answers anything but `404 not_found`" (plan lines 413-415) contradicts the tree.**
10	   - For an unknown id, `content_job` returns `(404, "not_found", "no such session")` (`src/app.rs:1856-1861`), and `remote_content` passes it on as a refusal (`:2093-2097`). So `sessions/<random uuid>/last-response` and `…/screen` answer exactly `404 not_found`.
11	   - As written, the test either fails or has to exempt the paths it exists to check. It needs seeded ids, or it needs to tell the allowlist's `"not available on this port"` refusal (`src/app.rs:3108-3114`) apart from a missing-record one.
12	
13	3. **Two line references do not match the worktree at 7fe8949.**
14	   - `bind_remote` is at `src/app.rs:2936`. The plan says `:2935` (line 348).
15	   - `Limits` is `src/adapters/remote.rs:623-639`. The plan says `:625-640` (line 262).
16	   - The others I checked hold: `:360`, `:389`, `:444-513`, `:519-527`, `:770`, `:95`, `:139,146`, `app.rs:3017`, `:3023`, `:3127-3153`, `:3568`, `:3606`, `:3754`, `core/remote.rs:46-72`, `:105-117`, `:166-175`, `ports/remote.rs:17`, `:26-42`, `:96-107`, `model.rs:12`, `:612`, `tests/remote.rs:245`, `:2892`, `:3226`, `tests/ui.rs:7424`, `Info.swift:114`.
17	
18	4. **The `IDENTITY_SCHEMA_VERSION` bump is never written for an existing installation.**
19	   - The plan sends `CertificateReissued` "through the existing `update_identity`" (plan lines 336-339). `update_identity` clones the identity and changes only what its closure changes (`src/core/remote.rs:105-117`). The only place that sets `schema_version` is `make_identity` (`src/adapters/remote.rs:118`).
20	   - So an upgraded `identity.json` gains `certificate_names` and `certificate_expires` but keeps `schema_version: 1`. The CLAUDE.md rule ("a schema bump for any serialized change") is then met only for fresh identities.
21	   - The `CertificateReissued` arm has to set `schema_version` to the new constant, and the core test the plan names (plan lines 396-397) should assert it.

1	# Plan: a web control surface on the remote port (#230)
2	
3	Line numbers are as they are in this worktree at 7fe8949. Schema versions
4	as they stand today: `SCHEMA_VERSION = 16` (`src/core/model.rs:12`),
5	`VIEWS_SCHEMA_VERSION = 7` (`:612`), `IDENTITY_SCHEMA_VERSION = 1`
6	(`src/ports/remote.rs:17`). Only the last moves, and it is written below

9	Unresolved N is in it.

11	## Where this departs from the issue
12	
13	- **"The one-line excerpt the card shows" is not on the wire.**
14	  `SessionView` (`control/src/lib.rs:636-688`) has no excerpt. The record
15	  has `last_message` (written by `src/bin/switchboard-hook.rs:37`;
16	  Settled, tree), but `remote-client.md` §4.3 says the excerpt is
17	  "masked from the turn's full text, then cut", and masking resolves the
18	  session's secret set, which §4.1 keeps off the frame. Putting
19	  `last_message` on `SessionView` would send unmasked text from a frame
20	  answer. So no `SessionView` change: the page fetches
21	  `sessions/{id}/last-response` for each Claude session, as the headset
22	  does (`client/Sources/SwitchboardUI/BrowserView.swift:149-163`), and
23	  only when that session's `last_stop_at_ms` differs from what it holds.
24	  No `watch` is registered for these, so the 128-key watch set is not
25	  touched by the list. Codex, shell, command and service rows show kind
26	  and state without an excerpt.
27	- **"The device's scope in the header": no endpoint returns it after
28	  pairing** (`remote_info`, `src/app.rs:3568`, is unauthenticated; the
29	  `/pair` reply is the only place, and it goes stale when the owner
30	  changes the scope in the dialog). The plan adds one authenticated read,
31	  `GET /api/v1/device`. This is the single new read model; the page
32	  cannot show a current scope without it.
33	- **"Revoked said plainly" cannot be told from "never paired" by the
34	  host's answer.** `authenticate` (`src/app.rs:3127-3153`) refuses both
35	  with `401 unauthorized`, and with an HttpOnly cookie the page cannot
36	  see whether it holds a token. The page keeps a non-secret marker
37	  (`server_id`, `device_id`, key hash, name) in `localStorage`. A 401
38	  with a marker says "This browser is no longer paired (it was revoked on
39	  the host, or the browser dropped its cookie). Pair again." A 401 with
40	  no marker says how to pair. "Identity changed, pair again" is the
41	  marker's `server_id` matching `/info` with a different key hash.
42	  No new refusal code.
43	- **"Any path outside `/api/v1/` is refused" is true but late:**
44	  `serve_remote` refuses it at `src/app.rs:3023`, after the request has
45	  taken a slot in the 64-deep channel and a frame pass. With a page, a
46	  browser sends strays (`/favicon.ico`, a prefetch). The connection
47	  thread now owns this decision: the three page paths are served there, any
48	  other path outside `/api/v1/` is answered 404 there, and `serve_remote`
49	  keeps its own refusal as the backstop.
50	- **"The browser then trusts that certificate for that address" is not
51	  safe to build on.** Settled (WebKit 41419, code-server's iPad doc): on
52	  Safari a click-through can cover the page and `fetch` but not `wss://`.
53	  The page therefore works on REST polling alone and treats the socket as
54	  an upgrade (decision 1 below).
55	- **"`history.replaceState` … the code never stays in the history" is
56	  stronger than the sources.** MDN (Settled) says `replaceState`
57	  replaces the current entry; it says nothing of what the browser
58	  recorded before the script ran (Unresolved 6). The plan makes the
59	  claim the host can keep: the code is single-use and the window closes
60	  at the first pairing, three failures or five minutes (Settled,
61	  `src/core/remote.rs:46-72`), so a recorded URL is dead. The dialog says
62	  that instead of promising the history is clean.

64	## The record
65	
66	No new record kind, no `model.rs` change, no `SCHEMA_VERSION` or
67	`VIEWS_SCHEMA_VERSION` bump. A browser is one more `PairedDevice`
68	(`src/ports/remote.rs:96-107`) in `devices.json`, which is a bare
69	`Vec<PairedDevice>` with no version. Its name is the page's `device_name`
70	("Safari on iPhone", built by the page from `navigator.userAgent`; the
71	host already cuts it to 64 characters, `new_device`,
72	`src/core/remote.rs:166-175`). No `kind` field: the name is enough for
73	the dialog (decision 6) and the host reads no `User-Agent`. Revoke and
74	scope change already apply on the next request and revoke closes the
75	socket.
76	
77	One record changes: `identity.json`. The certificate is reissued over the
78	same key (Settled: `KeyPair::from_pem` is already used,
79	`src/adapters/remote.rs:139,146`; the SPKI is of the key, so the pin
80	and `spki_sha256` do not move, §5). The reason is Settled (Apple's
81	rules): the current certificate has no subjectAltName, a CN only, no EKU,
82	and a `not_after` in the year 4096, so it meets none of the SAN, EKU or
83	825-day rules Safari applies. Reissuing cannot hurt the click-through
84	path and may help it (Unresolved 1, 2 and 3 are the open questions about
85	how much), so it does not wait on them. Two additive fields on `Identity`
86	(`src/ports/remote.rs:26-42`), both `#[serde(default)]`:
87	
88	- `certificate_names: Vec<String>`: the DNS and IP names the certificate
89	  carries, sorted.
90	- `certificate_expires: Option<SystemTime>`.
91	
92	Bump `IDENTITY_SCHEMA_VERSION` to the value in `ports/remote.rs` at
93	implementation time, plus one. `identity.json` has no migration step:
94	`load_identity` is a plain deserialize, so an older file reads with the
95	defaults (an empty list, `None`), which `bind_remote` treats as "reissue
96	now". Written through the existing atomic `RemoteFiles::save`.
97	
98	Rehydration is unchanged: `IdentityLoaded` at launch, devices by token
99	hash on every request. The pairing window stays non-durable. On the
100	device, what persists is the HttpOnly cookie (script cannot read it) and
101	the marker in `localStorage` (not secret: ids and a public key hash).
102	The cookie is the only place the token lives in the browser (decision 2).

104	## The signals
105	
106	### Decision 1: browser trust in the certificate
107	
108	**Picked: the click-through on the local network is the trust step, said
109	in the dialog. The host does not offer the certificate for download in
110	this cut.** Why: a download or profile install is a second trust
111	mechanism with its own surface (a route that serves a certificate before
112	pairing, a profile format, what iOS asks of a manually trusted
113	certificate), and the only evidence that it fixes `wss://` on Safari is
114	two sources of 2021 and 2026 (Settled), against Unresolved 1-3, which no
115	experiment here can settle. It is the follow-up if owner question A
116	comes back unfavourable (named at the end).
117	
118	What the click-through buys, and what it does not (the dialog says this
119	in two sentences, and §5 of the spec is amended to say it):
120	
121	- It lets the owner open the page. It proves nothing about who answered.
122	- The `key` in the URL lets the genuine page refuse to send the code to a
123	  host whose `/info` presents a different `spki_sha256`. That catches the
124	  right page on the wrong genuine host (a second installation on that
125	  address or port, a rotated key). A page served by an impostor is not a
126	  genuine page and checks nothing; a page cannot read the key of the TLS
127	  connection it is on, so even the genuine check proves only that the host
128	  claims that key. §5's sentence "a relayed request through a substituted
129	  certificate fails" stands for native clients and is amended: it does not
130	  hold for a browser.
131	- What bounds the damage: the code is single-use and short-lived
132	  (Settled), the pairing window shows scope, and the owner sees the new
133	  device in the dialog and can revoke it.
134	
135	The reissue (above) gives the certificate `serverAuth`, a validity of 800
136	days (under 825, Unresolved 3: if the rule does not bind a manually
137	trusted leaf, nothing is lost), and SANs for `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`,
138	the outward address from `local_address()` as an IP SAN, and, on macOS,
139	`<LocalHostName>.local` as a DNS SAN (Unresolved 2 and 9: both forms are
140	present, so whichever Safari accepts is there). The dialog says the
141	certificate is renewed (key, and so pin, unchanged) and that a changed
142	address means a new browser warning (Unresolved 7).
143	
144	The page's default is REST polling every 5 seconds plus a refetch of the
145	open session. When `new WebSocket` opens, the page switches to events
146	and stops polling; when it fails or closes, the page says "Live updates
147	unavailable, refreshing every 5 s" and polls. This is the same page
148	whether Unresolved 1 comes back favourable or not; the socket is the
149	enhancement, built behind the polling and not in front of it.
150	`crypto.randomUUID` is used only when `window.isSecureContext`, with a
151	`getRandomValues` fallback otherwise (Unresolved 4).
152	
153	### Decision 2: how the token reaches the host
154	
155	**Picked: an `HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict` cookie, set by the
156	`/pair` reply, carried by `fetch` and by the socket handshake. The page's
157	script never sees the token. Nothing in `localStorage`, no subprotocol
158	token.** That is the safer store (a script on the origin can read
159	`localStorage`; it cannot read an HttpOnly cookie), so it is the one this
160	plan builds. The facts file's Owner D says the server accepts all three
161	transports; this plan builds one (plus the bearer header the native
162	clients use) and does not build the other two.
163	
164	Mechanics that are unresolved are the implementer's first test, before
165	any other page code (Unresolved 5): on Safari, Chrome and Firefox with the
166	reissued certificate, does a `Secure` cookie set by `/pair` over an IP
167	host come back on a same-origin `fetch`? (This is the basic behaviour; the
168	`__Host-` prefix needs `Secure`, `Path=/`, no `Domain`, all met.) Does it
169	come back on a same-origin `new WebSocket` handshake? If the `fetch` half
170	fails, the finding goes to the owner as a follow-up and no
171	`localStorage` or subprotocol transport is added in this commit. If only
172	the socket half fails, nothing changes: the page polls (decision 1).
173	
174	Host side:
175	
176	- `read_request` (`src/adapters/remote.rs:444-513`) keeps three more
177	  headers, as the bearer is kept, so none are logged with the rest:
178	  `cookie`, `origin`, `host`. `RemoteRequest` (`:360`) gains
179	  `cookie: Option<String>`, `origin: Option<String>`,
180	  `host: Option<String>`. Settled: only `adapters/remote.rs` builds it,
181	  and no test constructs it.
182	- The token is the bearer if present, else the cookie named
183	  `__Host-sb-<server_id>` (per-installation name: Settled says cookies are
184	  not isolated by port, so two instances on one Mac would otherwise
185	  collide). `authenticate` (`src/app.rs:3127`) takes it from a new
186	  `RemoteRequest::token(&self, server_id)`; the cookie value is checked
187	  for length and base64url characters before it is hashed.
188	- **Origin check.** A cookie is ambient: `SameSite=Strict` is by site, and
189	  a site includes every port on the host, so another page on another port
190	  of this Mac is same-site. For a request authenticated by the cookie (no
191	  bearer), any method but GET and any WebSocket upgrade must carry an
192	  `Origin` equal to `https://` + the request's `Host` header, compared
193	  case-insensitively; otherwise `403 forbidden_origin`, no side effect.
194	  Comparing with the `Host` header, not a list of addresses, is what makes
195	  this correct for an IP, a `.local` name or loopback. Bearer-authenticated
196	  requests are exempt: a header is not ambient. This answers the owner
197	  question on `Origin`, and it is a security decision, so it is decided
198	  here.
199	- **`/pair`** (`remote_pair`, `src/app.rs:3606`) takes an additive body
200	  field `"transport": "cookie"`. With it the reply omits `token`, and
201	  `RemoteReply` carries `Set-Cookie: __Host-sb-<server_id>=<token>;
202	  Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Max-Age=34560000` (400 days,
203	  the longest browsers keep). Without it the reply is unchanged, so the
204	  CLI and the headset are untouched. `RemoteReply` (`:389`) gains
205	  `set_cookie: Option<String>` and `#[derive(Default)]`; Settled says it
206	  is built literally at about 15 sites in `src/app.rs` and none in `tests/`,
207	  so each literal gets `..RemoteReply::default()`, a mechanical edit.
208	- The cookie goes to every HTTPS service on that host, on any port
209	  (Settled). It is `HttpOnly`, so it cannot be read by script; it can be
210	  sent to a service the owner runs on the same Mac. The dialog says so, and
211	  it is named for the owner at the end.
212	
213	### Decision 3: one QR
214	
215	**One URL.** The pairing window's QR and "Copy invite" carry
216	`https://<ip>:<port>/?code=<code>&key=<spki_sha256>&id=<server_id>`,
217	built by one pure function in `src/core/remote.rs`,
218	`invite_url(address: SocketAddr, identity, code)`. It formats the address
219	through `SocketAddr`, so an IPv6 result gets its brackets (the JSON form
220	did not). Code, key and id are Crockford, hex and a UUID: nothing needs
221	percent-encoding. The JSON form is no longer emitted. Settled: the
222	visionOS paste field, `ConnectionManager.swift`, `BrowserView.swift:106,
223	883` and the CLI all go through `PairingInvite.parse`
224	(`client/Sources/SwitchboardProtocol/Info.swift:114`), so only that
225	changes: it tries `URLComponents` first (`code`, `key`, `id`, and
226	`addresses = ["host:port"]`) and the existing JSON decode second, so an
227	invite copied before the update still pairs. `addresses` stays a list
228	(`ConnectionManager.swift:483`, `main.swift:120`). The `.local` name is not
229	put in the URL: owner question B decides that, and the IP works whichever
230	way it comes back.
231	
232	### Decision 4: the static paths
233	
234	- **Paths, exactly:** `GET /` (also with a query), `GET /app.js`,
235	  `GET /app.css`. Content types `text/html; charset=utf-8`,
236	  `text/javascript; charset=utf-8`, `text/css; charset=utf-8`. The HTML
237	  carries `<link rel="icon" href="data:,">` so no `/favicon.ico` request is
238	  made. Any other method on these is `405` with `Allow: GET`; any other
239	  path outside `/api/v1/` is `404` with the usual JSON error.
240	- **Headers on all three (and the 404/405):** `Content-Security-Policy:
241	  default-src 'none'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; connect-src
242	  'self'; img-src data:; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none';
243	  frame-ancestors 'none'`, `Cache-Control: no-store`,
244	  `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` (the URL with the code must not leave in
245	  a `Referer`), `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Connection: close`.
246	  The page has no inline script, no inline style and no `style=` attribute,
247	  and no external URL. Whether WebKit treats `connect-src 'self'` as
248	  covering `wss://` on the same host is not in the facts; the first
249	  manual run on Safari records it, and the polling path is why a "no" does
250	  not break the page.
251	- **Who answers:** the connection thread (`connection`,
252	  `src/adapters/remote.rs:770`), before the request is handed to the
253	  frame, because the bytes need no core state and §4.1 says the frame does
254	  core state only. The bytes are `include_str!("../../web/index.html")`,
255	  `app.js`, `app.css` in `adapters/remote.rs`. No build step, no
256	  dependency.
257	- **Pool and rate window.** A page load counts against the 4
258	  unauthenticated connections like any stranger (§4.1; unchanged), and
259	  `Connection: close` frees the slot as soon as the file is sent, so the
260	  three files do not hold three slots for 30 s of idle (Unresolved 8: how
261	  many parallel connections iOS Safari opens needs a device). Static paths get
262	  their own `RateWindow` in `Limits` (`:625-640`), 60 per minute per
263	  listener, `429` past it, so a page-load loop cannot be charged to the
264	  `/pair` window (6/min) or the `/info` window (60/min). The page's own
265	  `/info` and `/pair` calls count against theirs as today.
266	- **Before pairing the listener serves `/info`, `/pair` and the page.**
267	  §5's "Require pairing before anything but `/info` and `/pair`" is
268	  amended to add the page. The page's bytes are identical on every
269	  installation and carry no host data (no id, no key, no name): the
270	  host-specific values arrive only in the URL the owner scanned and in
271	  `/info`.
272	- **Opened with neither code nor marker:** a plain message: "Open
273	  Remote devices in Switchboard on the Mac, choose Allow pairing, and scan
274	  the code with this device's camera." No code-entry form in this cut: a
275	  typed code without the scanned key would skip the one check the page
276	  can make. A paste field is the natural follow-up.
277	- **`refuse` and the code.** The page request never reaches the frame, so
278	  `refuse` (`src/app.rs:3754`, logs method and path only) is not on the
279	  path; the static arm logs nothing and never logs the query.
